subject: [enc4k] HEVC reopen ROOT CAUSE found + fixed (guest heap): restarts no longer needed; pipelining verdict; HEIC_HW_PLAN.md
body: (1) Reproduced on the host runner (two AP sessions in one process): H.264->H.264 OK, HEVC->HEVC: 2nd frame never completes, vendor log '[Error] too many GCE buffers !' x6. Vendor code: h264_enc_init and hevc_enc_init both malloc(0x5ab10) for the encoder handle; h264 clears all of it, hevc_enc_init clears only 0x424 bytes. VENC_gceResourceInit then puts 3 GCE command buffers per core into a 3-slot list INSIDE that handle (handle+0x58cc0, slots +0x18) and refuses when the slots are non-zero. On Android a 370 KB malloc is a fresh zeroed mapping; our V30 guest heap recycled the freed block (the previous session's handle, H.264 or HEVC, same size) with its old slots -> the HEVC frame's GCE buffers are never queued -> hang (vc18 H.264->HEVC seq-hdr -60, vc24/vc25 HEVC->HEVC frame 0). Fix: shim/n2shim_heap.c zeroes recycled blocks >= 64 KiB (bionic semantics). Host: 3x HEVC and h264,hevc,h264,hevc in one process all OK, 0 errors; V30 277637/277637 (+zero-on-reuse check), IP 1088/1088. payload-vcodec-reopen (vcodecd 8ba58f7c, keepalive WITHOUT --restart-on-switch, stage-vcodec.sh --no-restart): avc1 1080p High -> hvc1 1080p -> hvc1 4K -> avc1 4K -> hvc1 1080p60 -> avc1 720p, ONE process. (2) Pipelining one stream across the two cores is not possible: consecutive frames depend on each other (P-frame references the previous reconstruction); the core 0/1 alternation is the vendor's buffer ping-pong, and the Linux driver also encodes one frame at a time per instance. Two cores can only overlap for independent streams (two sessions) or intra-only work (HEIC tiles). 4K60 P-frame HEVC is therefore capped at ~40 fps by the 25.6 ms/frame (624 MHz); remaining levers: --venc-keep-power, per-frame overhead. No async flush implemented (would not help video). (3) gpu/hwcodec/HEIC_HW_PLAN.md: the vendor ALSO has a HEIF encoder type (fourcc HEIF, IPI 17, up to 16383x16383, heif_grid_size param) besides H265 (3840x2176); first step = logging proxy around VCPHEVC to see what CMPhoto calls; estimate 12 MP ~120-190 ms one core / ~50-110 ms with HEIF mode or two cores vs 1586 ms software.
